original_value: We give a survey on recent advances at the forefront of research on probabilistic knowledge bases for representing and querying large-scale automatically extracted data. We concentrate especially on increasing the semantic expressivity of formalisms for representing and querying probabilistic knowledge (i) by giving up the closed-world assumption, (ii) by allowing for commonsense knowledge (and in parallel giving up the tuple-independence assumption), and (iii) by giving up the closed-domain assumption, while preserving some computational properties of query answering in such formalisms.

result.paraphrase: We present a survey of recent advances at the cutting edge of research on probabilistic knowledge bases for representing and querying large-scale automatically extracted data. In particular, we focus on expanding the semantic expressivity of formalisms for representing and querying probabilistic knowledge by (i) abandoning the closed-world assumption, (ii) permitting commonsense knowledge while also abandoning tuple independence, and (iii) abandoning the closed-domain assumption, all while retaining some computational properties of query answering in these formalisms.
